title: strtok in C eats your string alive
description:
strtok looks like a friendly string splitter, but it mutates your buffer in place and hides its progress in a static variable. Here's exactly what it does to your array, why a string literal is undefined behavior, and why two strtok loops can't run at once. From the C Mastery Path lesson on multi-dimensional arrays and string manipulation.

Source lesson(s):
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/c-mastery-path/level-2/03-multidim-arrays-strings/

#Shorts

beats.narration: You split a string in C with strtok. Every field comes out fine. Then you print the original string, and most of it is gone.
Here's the split. strtok hands back one comma-separated field at a time until it returns NULL.
But it never copies. Each time it hits a comma, it overwrites that comma with a null terminator, right inside your array. Afterward the string stops at the first field.
Two rules. Never pass strtok a string literal, that's undefined behavior. And it keeps its place in a hidden static variable, so two strtok loops can't run at once.
Need the original intact? Split a copy instead. Fields out, data kept.
Full breakdown's in the C Mastery Path lesson on multi-dimensional arrays and strings.
